newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan plans air links with Russia, India.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan plans air links with Russia, India.

text.p: Taiwan said on Friday it was stepping up efforts to forge air links with Russia, India and other countries that recognise the island's rival, China.
"We will send a delegation to Moscow around March 2 for working-level talks with Russia on March 5-6," said Wang Wei-chieh, the foreign ministry's West Asian affairs director.

The sides agreed in principle in 1993 to forge air links and the delegation would discuss issues concerning direct flight services and extension of flights beyond Taipei and Moscow, Wang told Reuters.
China Airlines, Taiwan's largest carrier, and Russia's TransAero would be designated to operate the flights, he said.

Despite the 1993 agreement, direct flights have been stalled by doubts about profitability and the certainty of protests from China, which views Taiwan as a renegade province ineligible for participation in international affairs.
Beijing protested to Russia after the 1993 pact was agreed.
Earlier this month, China expressed anger at a secret aviation pact between Cambodia and Taiwan, which plans to commence flights from Taipei to Phnom Penh at the end of March.

A China Airlines official acknowledged that the carrier was bound to lose money if it could only fly the Taipei-Moscow route. If China Airlines were allowed to extend its flights to other European destinations, it would help business, she said.
Wang said the delegation would strive for such extensions during the talks.

In addition to the likely air links with Russia, Taiwan was negotiating with India for an aviation pact that would allow airlines from both sides to start direct flights, said Transport Minister Tsai Chao-yang.
"We are seeking to establish air links with India this year," Tsai said without elaborating.
Aviation officials said Taiwan also sought to hold talks with Burma for possible air links.
